result:
I added `requireActor(id)` to `src/users.js`. It looks the user up and throws `unknown actor: <id>` or `actor has no role: <id>`, using the same messages and checks in the same order as before. The 17 existing tests pass, though I didn't add tests that hit the refusal paths directly.

- **`createExpense`** (`src/expenses.js`) and **`approveExpense`** (`src/approvals.js`) now call it instead of their own copy.
- **`POST /expenses`** (`src/routes.js`) now calls `requireActor` too. `createExpense` already does the same check first, so I could have deleted the route's copy. I kept a call there so the route still refuses a bad actor before doing anything else, as it did before.
- **`rejectExpense`** is unchanged. It only checks that the user exists, not that they have a role, so a user with no role can still reject an expense today. Using the helper there would have started refusing that user. If the missing check is a bug, switching it over is a one-line change, but it would change behaviour, so I left it for you to decide.

For the two new call sites, call `requireActor(actorId)`.
